study_identification.title: Dissecting task-based fMRI activity using normative modelling: an application to the Emotional Face Matching Task

study_characteristics.study_objective: To demonstrate the potential of normative modelling to identify individual differences in task-based fMRI using the Emotional Face Matching Task (EFMT), and to map deviations in patients with mental health conditions relative to a reference cohort.

dataset_name.answer: Human Connectome Project (HCP) Young Adult, HCP Development, UK Biobank, Amsterdam Open MRI Collection Population Imaging of Psychology (AOMIC PIOP2), Duke Neurogenetics Study (DNS), and MIND-Set.

hc_sex.answer: See Table 1. HCP Young Adult: 561 F (53.7%); HCP Development: 110 F (54.7%); UK Biobank: 2495 F (49.9%); AOMIC PIOP2: 114 F (57.0%); DNS: 707 F (56.7%); MIND-Set (Reference): 21 F (56.7%).

quality_checking_detail.answer: Participants were excluded if their mean relative RMS was greater than 0.5 mm. Additional quality control was performed for signal coverage in the prefrontal cortex for the UK Biobank sample.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: We included dummy coded site-related variables as additional covariates of no-interest.

response_variable.answer: z-statistic maps from the contrast face>shapes and face>baseline.

predictor_variables.answer: site, age, sex, intra-cranial volume, and acquisition [TR, multiband sequence, number of volumes collected (per run where applicable)] and task parameters [task length (in seconds, and per run where applicable), number of target blocks, instructions for faces condition, and the target stimuli (i.e. which stimulus set they came from)].

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.answer: Yes. The model included covariates for site, acquisition and task parameters.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.answer: Yes. The data was split into training and test sets.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.answer: Yes. An additional out-of-sample test was performed with 5000 UK Biobank participants.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.answer: Yes. The model was applied to a clinical cohort (MIND-Set).

diseases_studied.answer: Mood and anxiety disorders, autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and/or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Sparse canonical correlation analyses (SCCA) to relate deviation scores to transdiagnostic functional domains.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative modelling of fMRI task-activation can illustrate the influence of different task choices and map replicable individual differences.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Patients have a higher frequency of extreme deviations for the face>shapes contrast, which are spatially heterogeneous. Normative models for faces>baseline have greater predictive value for individuals' transdiagnostic functioning.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Under-representation of participants in mid-adulthood (37-46 years). Collinearity of predictor variables across sites.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates the potential of normative modeling to dissect heterogeneity in task-fMRI data and its clinical relevance.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a comprehensive demonstration of applying normative modeling to task-based fMRI data, highlighting its advantages over traditional case-control approaches.
